subject: Observability add-on credits — annual bucket exchange and bulk discount options
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@spacely-aviation.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability add-on — can we apply annual bucket to cover spikes?

Hi Soojin / Laura,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the new tracing UI looks promising. We ran the usage workbook against our Q1 and Q2 ingest patterns (attached) and we have two asks before Procurement will greenlight a pilot:

1) Can Redwood allow an "annual bucket exchange" for observability credits so that committed credits (for dashboards/tracing/retention) can be used flexibly across ingestion spikes? Right now our spikes in troubleshooting months would otherwise cause large overages.

2) Second, what's the best path to a bulk discount on the observability module if we commit to a 12-month spend that includes a moderate uplift in consumption — procuring on behalf of three internal teams. Procurement is explicitly asking for a discount schedule tied to committed credit bands (e.g., 0-100k tokens, 100k-500k, 500k+).

Attached: Spacely_telemetry_usage_2025.xlsx (workbook with month-by-month ingest)

Would appreciate a short note with options and the simplest SOW path so we can review with Legal / Procurement.

Thanks,
Alicia
Head of Observability Programs
Spacely Aviation

--
Attachment: Spacely_telemetry_usage_2025.xlsx (xlsx, 540KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 12:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability add-on — can we apply annual bucket to cover spikes?

Hi Alicia — thanks for the workbook, that helped. High level options below — happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through numbers.

Option A — Annual bucket with smoothing credits (recommended)- You purchase a 12-month committed observability bucket (tokens/ingest units) that we apportion monthly. We apply a smoothing policy that can draw up to 2x the monthly apportioned units during spikes by consuming from the remaining annual bucket first. No overage until the annual bucket is exhausted.

Option B — Tiered committed bands + capped overage- Commit to a band (e.g., 100k / 300k / 750k) with stepped discounts at each band; overage billed at standard rates but with a 10% cap.

Commercials I can offer today for a 12-month commit (subject to final SOW):
- Intro concession: 18% off list for observability add-ons on first-year committed dollars if you commit to the 300k band (payable monthly or prepaid)
- Rollover: unused portion of annual bucket can roll forward for up to 2 months after term end for operational continuity

Next steps we usually take:
1) I’ll draft a short SOW that embeds the bucket definition and smoothing policy.
2) Pricing team locks final banding and discounts (Ben is looped).
3) DocuSign SOW -> Pilot kickoff.

I’ve attached a starter SOW (SOW-Spacely-observability-v1.3.docx) and a quick pricing cheatsheet for Ben to validate.

If that sounds reasonable, can you confirm which billing model Procurement prefers (prepay vs monthly amortized)? Prepay increases the concession flexibility.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability add-on — can we apply annual bucket to cover spikes?

Soojin — quick internal note and suggested guardrails before we put legal on the SOW:

1) Approver threshold: I can approve up to a 15% concession for first-year deals under $200k ARR. Above that band we need RevOps + CRO signoff. The 18% you proposed for the 300k band is slightly outside my approval; we should present a tiered concession (15% at 100k band, 18% at 300k with finance signoff).

2) Cost impact: smoothing that pulls from the annual bucket is fine, but we need a protection clause: if monthly peak usage > 5x baseline for two consecutive months we convert to a temporary premium overage rate to protect utilization. We can surface that in the SOW as an exception.

3) Alternative compromise: offer 15% discount on committed dollars + a one-time "surge credit" equal to 5% of committed dollars to be consumed in months of spike. That keeps it simple for Procurement.

I attached the pricing cheat with suggested math and sample invoice line items. If Alicia signals prepay we can be more aggressive with concession.

Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: pricing-cheatsheet.csv (csv, 12KB)

1) Final SOW with the smoothing language and the exception clause Ben mentioned (conversion to premium rate if consecutive large peaks). Can you send a Word/PDF we can share with Legal?
2) A sample invoice line (monthly amortization and a prepaid option) so our AP team can confirm payment terms. Also confirm whether the "surge credit" is consumed automatically during spike months or requires a formal request.

If we can get the SOW and sample invoice today we’ll target a Procurement review on Monday and aim to sign the SOW by end of next week. Pilot target start: July 1.
